proposed.sourceName: Islam Q&A — Fatwa 11609 'Eating beef that has not been slaughtered properly'
proposed.paraphrase: Rules that meat from an animal killed without proper Islamic slaughter (e.g. by stunning, strangulation, or a blow) is maytah and haram per Quran 16:115, whether done by Muslims or others; the People-of-the-Book allowance applies only to meat actually slaughtered by a lawful method.

proposed.sourceName: About Islam — 'Can I Eat Meat not Islamically Slaughtered?' (Dr. Muhammad Salah, Shari'ah Academy)
proposed.paraphrase: Holds non-Islamically-slaughtered meat forbidden except meat of the People of the Book slaughtered by an actual cut with Allah's name invoked — excluding animals killed by shooting, suffocation or strangulation and anything slaughtered in another name; since modern industrial conditions often fail these, unspecified non-zabiha meat must be verified and is otherwise avoided.
